technical_and_design_decisions: Target the Spring XD codebase (per referenced branch for U1) as the implementation platform; the broader Spring Framework context is background only.
For U1, retain backward compatibility of BaseDefinition's public API by introducing an internal reparse hook rather than a breaking signature change.
For U2, implement reliable HDFS writes by leveraging Hadoop's Syncable API (hflush/hsync) and tying acknowledgment to a successful sync, not just stream closure.
For U3, expose partition selection through a new PartitionStrategy interface that source/processor modules can implement; default implementation preserves existing round-robin behavior.
For U4, model consumption of multiple topic-partitions using a composite consumer that fans in to a single internal queue without changing downstream module contracts.

For U5, design the new DSL parser as a two-phase parser (lex/scan + a symbol-table-aware resolve phase) so cross-stream references (e.g. 'MyStream' above) can be resolved at parse time, with clear diagnostics for invalid module/option values.
For U6, focus on architecture design and an ADR-style document describing single-container colocation of stream modules; do not implement runtime changes.
For U7, fix deserialization by stashing the ConfigurableConversionService as an explicit tuple field rather than relying on implicit environment rebinding after restart.
For U8, design a reproducible benchmark harness (e.g. JMH or fixed-rate producer) with a single environment and toggleable JMX, then capture and report results.
Use the existing Spring XD build (Maven), test stack (JUnit/Spring TestContext), and CI pipeline; no new infrastructure is introduced.
Perform all work in a single developer capacity using 8-hour workdays; no team coordination overhead is included beyond documented design alignment.
assumptions: The reference branch referenced in U1 is available and the codebase is buildable locally.
Existing module/stream abstractions (Module, Stream, ModuleDeployer, etc.) are stable and reusable.
Hadoop and Kafka client libraries are already on the classpath at compatible versions.
A representative cluster (or local equivalent) is available to validate U2 and U4 behavior end-to-end.
The Flo UI side of U5 requires only the parser-side change; UI integration is out of scope for this increment.
U6 deliverable is design + documentation only; no production runtime code change is required.
Benchmarking in U8 is done against the developer's local or single-node environment; distributed benchmarking is not included.
An 'activity' in this WBS is one logical work item performed by the lone developer; estimates include design, implementation, and unit-test effort but exclude calendar elapsed time.
Effort figures are most-likely (single-point) estimates in workdays; no contingency buffer is added at the activity level.

activities.activity_name: Requirements analysis and overall technical design
activities.activity_description: Read each user story, map dependencies across U1–U8, draft the overall module structure, design notes, and confirm the technical decisions that drive downstream activities.
Remove the eager list of modules from BaseDefinition, add a reparse entry point that re-resolves modules on demand, update callers, and adjust unit tests accordingly.

activities.activity_name: U2: Reliable HDFS writes with commit acknowledgment
activities.activity_description: Extend the HDFS sink to call hsync/hflush and surface an acknowledgment to the message bus only after a confirmed HDFS commit; add failure handling and tests.

activities.activity_name: U3: Overridable partition function in source/processor
activities.activity_description: Introduce a PartitionStrategy hook in source/processor modules, wire it through the MessageChannel, and verify the default behavior is preserved.

activities.activity_name: U4: Consume multiple topic-partitions into a single queue
activities.activity_description: Implement a multi-partition Kafka consumer that merges records into one internal queue while preserving ordering guarantees required by stream pipelines; add tests.

activities.activity_name: U5: New DSL parser for Flo
activities.activity_description: Design and implement a new DSL parser with a symbol-table resolution phase that understands previously defined streams, returning clear errors for invalid module/option values; add parser tests including the MyStream example.

activities.activity_name: U6: Design and document single-container stream deployment
activities.activity_description: Produce an architecture/design document covering colocation of modules in a single container: lifecycle, isolation, scaling implications, and trade-offs. No runtime code change.

activities.activity_name: U7: Uniform handling of ConfigurableConversionService tuples
activities.activity_description: Investigate deserialization loss of non-default ConfigurableConversionService, persist the service reference as part of tuple state, and verify it is not reset after restart; add regression tests.

activities.activity_name: U8: Benchmark stream with and without JMX
activities.activity_description: Build a reproducible benchmark harness, run the same stream scenario with JMX enabled and disabled, capture metrics, and document the performance differences.
Run end-to-end integration tests covering interactions among U1–U5 and U7 (e.g. a stream that uses U3 partition override with U4 multi-partition source and a U2 HDFS sink).

activities.activity_name: Documentation, release notes, and final cleanup
activities.activity_description: Update reference documentation, write release notes summarizing the new capabilities, and perform final code review cleanup before delivery.
